h: חַג הַפֶּסַח, מַאֲמָר ט״ו Pesach — Maamar Tes Vav
From the Morrow of the Shabbos: The Barley Omer, the Four Cups and Haman's Accusation

p: לֵיל שֵׁנִי
Second Night
יוֹם טוֹב זֶה נִקְרָא בַּתּוֹרָה "שַׁבָּת" סְתָם, כְּמוֹ שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
This festival (the first day of Pesach) is called in the Torah simply "Shabbos," as it is said
(וַיִּקְרָא כ"ג, ט"ו):
(Vayikra 23:15):
מִמָּחֳרַת הַשַּׁבָּת,
"From the morrow of the Shabbos,"
וְזֶה גָּרַם לַבַּיְיתוֹסִים לִטְעוֹת שֶׁעֲצֶרֶת אַחַר הַשַּׁבָּת
which caused the Boethusians to err in thinking that Shavuos always falls after a weekly Shabbos
(מְנָחוֹת ס"ה.).
(Menachos 65a).
וְלָמָּה לֹא נִכְתַּב בַּתּוֹרָה "מִמָּחֳרַת הַפֶּסַח", שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֲרִיכוּת לָשׁוֹן גַּם כֵּן?
Now why was it not written in the Torah "from the morrow of Pesach," which is no longer in wording either?
וְהָעִנְיָן הוּא דְּשַׁבָּת הוּא לְשׁוֹן נַיְּיחָא,
The explanation is that "Shabbos" denotes serenity (naycha),
שֶׁבִּכְנִיסַת הַשַּׁבָּת כְּתִיב
for at the onset of the first Shabbos it is written
(בְּרֵאשִׁית א', ל"א):
(Bereishis 1:31):
וַיַּרְא אֱלֹהִים אֶת כָּל אֲשֶׁר עָשָׂה וְהִנֵּה טוֹב מְאֹד,
"And God saw all that He had made, and behold, it was very good"
שֶׁמָּצָא ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ נַיְּיחָא בְּהַבְּרִיאָה,
meaning that Hashem, may He be blessed, found serenity in Creation,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה ט', ד'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 9:4):
עוֹלָמִי עוֹלָמִי, הַלְוַאי תְּהֵא מַעֲלֶת חֵן לְפָנַי תָּמִיד כְּשֵׁם שֶׁהֶעֱלֵיתָ חֵן לְפָנַי בְּשָׁעָה זוֹ.
"My world, My world, would that you always find favor before Me just as you have found favor before Me at this moment."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁצָּפָה שֶׁהַכֹּל הָיָה כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹב מְאֹד,
That is, He foresaw that everything was designed so that it would become "very good,"
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁמּוּבָא
as brought
(זֹהַר חֵלֶק ב' קפ"ד.)
(Zohar, Vol. 2, 184a)
דְּלֵית נְהוֹרָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא, וְלֵית טָבָא אֶלָּא הַהוּא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ בִּישָׁא.
that there is no light except that which emerges from darkness, and no good except that which emerges from evil.
אֲבָל אָז הָיָה רַק שֶׁצָּפָה הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא שֶׁיִּהְיֶה אוּמָּה יִשְׂרָאֵלִית וִיקַבְּלוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ בְּשַׁבָּת וְיַנִּיחוּ כָּל עִסְקֵיהֶם לִכְבוֹדוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ,

However, back at Creation, the Holy One, blessed is He, only foresaw that there would arise an Israelite nation who would accept the yoke of His kingship on Shabbos and lay aside all their affairs for His honor, may He be blessed
וְזֶה תַּכְלִית מַעֲשֵׂה שָׁמַיִם וָאָרֶץ,
and this is the ultimate purpose of the making of heaven and earth,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ:
as they said:
יָמִים יֻצָּרוּ וְלוֹ אֶחָד בָּהֶם — זֶה יוֹם הַשַּׁבָּת
"'Days were fashioned, and to Him is one among them'—this is the Shabbos day"
(תַּנָּא דְּבֵי אֵלִיָּהוּ רַבָּה פֶּרֶק א').
(Tanna D'vei Eliyahu Rabbah, Chapter 1).
אֲבָל עִיקַּר הַנַּיְּיחָא הָיָה בִּיצִיאַת מִצְרַיִם, שֶׁכְּבָר הָיָה אוּמָּה שְׁלֵימָה, כְּנֶסֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל, שֶׁקִּבְּלוּ עוֹל מַלְכוּתוֹ,
Yet the primary serenity was realized at the Exodus from Egypt, when there already existed a complete nation, Knesses Yisrael, who accepted the yoke of His kingship,
וְאָז מָצָא ה' יִתְבָּרַךְ נַיְּיחָא בְּעוֹלָמוֹ.
and then Hashem, may He be blessed, found actual serenity in His world.
וְנִקְרָא "שַׁבָּת" בְּפָרָשַׁת הָעוֹמֶר,
And it is specifically called "Shabbos" in the section of the Omer offering,
שֶׁכֵּן הִקְרִיבוּ אָז הָעוֹמֶר מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִים שֶׁהוּא מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה,
for then they offered the Omer from barley, which is animal fodder,
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
as they said
(פְּסָחִים ג':):
(Pesachim 3b):
שְׂעוֹרִין נַעֲשׂוּ יָפוֹת וְכוּלֵּי, צֵא וּבַשֵּׂר לַסּוּסִים וְלַחֲמוֹרִים,
"The barley has grown well, etc.—go and bring good tidings to the horses and donkeys,"
וְכֵן
and likewise
(סוֹטָה י"ד.):
(Sotah 14a):
כְּשֵׁם שֶׁמַּעֲשֶׂיהָ מַעֲשֵׂה בְּהֵמָה כָּךְ קָרְבָּנָהּ מַאֲכַל בְּהֵמָה
"Just as her deed was the deed of a beast, so her offering is animal food"
וְהוּא לְהוֹרוֹת שֶׁאַף מַעֲשֵׂה בְּהֵמָה, שֶׁהוּא הַהִיפּוּךְ מֵהַטּוֹב וְהַחֹשֶׁךְ שֶׁהוּא מַעֲשֵׂיהֶן שֶׁל רְשָׁעִים,
which comes to teach that even animalistic behavior—the very opposite of good, and the darkness that is the deeds of the wicked
הוּא כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹב מְאֹד, נְהוֹרָא מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא;
exists so that there may be "very good," light emerging from darkness;
וְלָכֵן דַּיְיקָא בְּפָרָשַׁת הָעוֹמֶר נִקְרָא יוֹם טוֹב זֶה "שַׁבָּת" סְתָם.
and therefore specifically in the section of the Omer is this festival called unqualified "Shabbos."

Rashi has no comment on these words.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: R. Shneur Zalman of Liadi, Likkutei Torah, Emor 3 — “Nullifying the animal soul came through waving the Omer and counting the Omer: ‘And he shall wave the Omer before Hashem for your favor; on the morrow of the Shabbos the Kohen shall wave it.’ For the Omer is of barley, which is animal fodder, and correspondingly above there is also an aspect of ‘beast.’ And this is why it says ‘on the morrow of the Shabbos’ and not ‘on the morrow of Yom Tov,’ for it is above the level of Shabbos, so that through the counting the animal soul too is transformed and your own will is nullified.” Connection: The Alter Rebbe also reads the Omer of animal fodder, and the Torah's calling the day “Shabbos” in that passage, as the raising of what is beastlike in Israel; Rav Tzadok sees in it the light that comes out of darkness.

Barley as animal fodder: light from darkness

p: וְתִיקְּנוּ חֲכָמִים בְּחַג זֶה אַרְבָּעָה כּוֹסוֹת,
And the Sages instituted on this festival Four Cups of wine,
וְהוּא שִׁיעוּר שִׁכְרוּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
which is a measure of intoxication, as they said
(כְּתוּבּוֹת ס"ה.):
(Kesubos 65a):
אַרְבָּעָה — אֲפִילּוּ חֲמוֹר תּוֹבַעַת בַּשּׁוּק וְאֵינָהּ מַקְפֶּדֶת.
"With four cups, even a donkey she demands in the marketplace and is uninhibited."
וְלֹא מָצִינוּ שֶׁיִּהְיֶה מִצְוָה בְּשִׁכְרוּת זוּלַת בְּפוּרִים, דְּאִיתָא
Now we do not find a mitzvah of intoxication anywhere else except on Purim, where it is stated
(מְגִילָּה ז':):
(Megillah 7b):
מִיחַיֵּיב אִינִישׁ לִבְסוּמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא וְכוּלֵּי,
"A person is obligated to become mellow with wine on Purim, etc."
וְשָׁם הַטַּעַם מִפְּנֵי שֶׁהַיְּשׁוּעָה הָיְתָה לְמַעְלָה מִתְּפִיסַת שֵׂכֶל בְּנֵי אָדָם
and there the reason is because the salvation transcended human intellectual grasp
אֲבָל בְּמָקוֹם אַחֵר לֹא מָצִינוּ מִצְוָה בְּשִׁכְרוּת.
but elsewhere we do not find a mitzvah of intoxication.
אַךְ סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת מָצִינוּ רִאשׁוֹנָה אֵצֶל יוֹסֵף שֶׁעָשָׂה לַשְּׁבָטִים סְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ
However, we first find a Shabbos meal with Yosef, who prepared a Shabbos meal for the tribes, as they said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית רַבָּה צ"ב, ד'):
(Bereishis Rabbah 92:4):
"וְהָכֵן" — אֵין הָכֵן אֶלָּא שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵּי,
"'And prepare (v'hachein)'—preparation refers only to Shabbos, etc."
וְשָׁם נֶאֱמַר
and there it is said
(בְּרֵאשִׁית מ"ג, ל"ד):
(Bereishis 43:34):
וַיִּשְׁתּוּ וַיִּשְׁכְּרוּ עִמּוֹ.
"And they drank and became intoxicated with him."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁרָצָה לֵידַע אִם הַשְּׁבָטִים גַּם כֵּן מְבוֹרָרִים,
That is, he wanted to know whether the tribes were also completely refined,
שֶׁבִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָדָם נִיכָּר: בְּכוֹסוֹ
for in three things a person's true character is revealed: in his cup (drinking)
(עֵירוּבִין ס"ה:),
(Eruvin 65b),
וְכֵן בִּסְעוּדַת שַׁבָּת נִתְבָּרְרוּ יִשְׂרָאֵל נֶגֶד הָאוּמּוֹת, כִּדְאִיתָא
and likewise at a Shabbos meal Israel are distinguished from the nations, as stated
(מְגִילָּה י"ב:):
(Megillah 12b):
בְּיוֹם הַשְּׁבִיעִי — שַׁבָּת הָיָה, שֶׁיִּשְׂרָאֵל אוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין וְכוּלֵּי;
"On the seventh day—it was Shabbos, when Israel eat and drink, etc.";
רָצָה יוֹסֵף לֵידַע אִם הַשְּׁבָטִים גַּם כֵּן מְבוֹרָרִים בַּלֵּב.
so Yosef wanted to know if the tribes were also purified in heart.
וְהַיַּיִן יְשַׂמַּח לְבַב אֱנוֹשׁ
And "wine gladdens the heart of frail man (enosh)"
וְהַיְינוּ אַף מִי שֶׁפָּגַם וְקִלְקֵל, שֶׁכֵּן נִדְרָשׁ
meaning even one who blemished and sinned, for thus it is expounded
(שַׁבָּת קי"ח:):
(Shabbos 118b):
אַשְׁרֵי אֱנוֹשׁ — שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ עוֹבֵד עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה כֶּאֱנוֹשׁ מוֹחֲלִין לוֹ.
"'Fortunate is enosh'—that even one who worships idols like Enosh is forgiven."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁעַל יְדֵי שַׁבָּת מְתַקְּנִים הֶעָבָר.
That is, through Shabbos the past is rectified.
וִישַׂמַּח — הַיְינוּ: לְיִשְׁרֵי לֵב שִׂמְחָה,
And "gladdens" refers to "for the upright of heart, joy"
שֶׁזּוֹכִין לְיִשְׁרֵי הַלֵּב, שֶׁיִּהְיוּ שְׁנֵי הַלְּבָבוֹת רַק טוֹב, וּלְהוֹרִיק הָרַע מִלֵּב כְּסִיל, וְיִהְיֶה הַכֹּל טוֹב מְאֹד.
that they merit uprightness of heart, so that both chambers of the heart are purely good, emptying the evil from the fool's heart, and everything becomes "very good."

וְלָכֵן בְּפָרָשַׁת הָעוֹמֶר שֶׁבָּא מִן הַשְּׂעוֹרִים, שֶׁהוּא לְבָרֵר שֶׁאַף מִי שֶׁמַּעֲשָׂיו מַעֲשֵׂה בְּהֵמָה מִכָּל מָקוֹם הוּא רַק כְּדֵי שֶׁיִּהְיֶה טוֹב מְאֹד, נְהוֹרָא דְּנָפִיק מִגּוֹ חֲשׁוֹכָא,
And therefore in the section of the Omer—which comes from barley to demonstrate that even one whose deeds are beast-like exists solely so that there be "very good," light emerging from darkness
בְּפָרָשָׁה זוֹ דַּיְיקָא נִקְרָא חַג זֶה בְּשֵׁם "שַׁבָּת" סְתָם.
specifically in this section is this festival called unqualified "Shabbos."
וּבָא בּוֹ גַּם כֵּן הַיַּיִן בְּשִׁיעוּר שִׁכְרוּת לְבָרֵר אֶת יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁנִּיכָּר בְּכוֹסוֹ,
And wine also comes on it in a measure of intoxication to refine Israel, who are tested in their cup,
שֶׁבְּיִשְׂרָאֵל הַיַּיִן זָכָה מְשַׂמְּחוֹ, כְּמוֹ שֶׁאָמְרוּ בְּיוֹמָא
for with Israel, if one is worthy, wine gladdens him, as they said in Yoma
שֶׁזּוֹכֶה לְיַשְׁרוּת הַלֵּב.
meaning he merits uprightness of heart.
וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ שֶׁבְּחַג זֶה בָּא הָאֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה שֶׁמְּבָרְכִין עָלֶיהָ "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ",
And as we have explained, on this festival eating is elevated into holiness over which we bless "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us,"
שֶׁבָּא לְתַקֵּן שׁוֹרֶשׁ הַפְּגַם שֶׁהָיָה בַּאֲכִילָה וְנִתְקַלֵּל: וְאָכַלְתָּ אֶת עֵשֶׂב הַשָּׂדֶה,
which comes to rectify the root of the original blemish in eating, when man was cursed with "And you shall eat the grass of the field"
וְעַל זֶה בָּא הַשִּׁינּוּי בְּטִיבּוּל יְרָקוֹת שֶׁזֶּה הָיָה סִיבָּה לְוַיְמָרְרוּ אֶת חַיֵּיהֶם בַּעֲבֹדָה קָשָׁה,
and concerning this comes the unusual act of dipping vegetables, which was the cause of "And they embittered their lives with hard labor,"
וְאַחֲרֵי זֶה בָּא הַמִּצְוָה בַּאֲכִילַת מַצָּה שֶׁהוּא בִּיטּוּל הַשְּׂאוֹר שֶׁבָּעִיסָּה.
and after that comes the mitzvah of eating matzah, which is the nullification of the leaven in the dough.
וּמְבָרְכִין עַל הָאֲכִילוֹת "אֲשֶׁר קִדְּשָׁנוּ בְּמִצְוֹתָיו וְצִוָּנוּ", שֶׁזֶּה גּוּפֵיהּ מֵבִיא קְדוּשָּׁה לְיִשְׂרָאֵל,
And we recite "Who has sanctified us with His commandments and commanded us" over these acts of eating, for this itself infuses holiness into Israel,
וְעַל יְדֵי זֶה מְתַקְּנִים כָּל אֲכִילוֹת שֶׁל כָּל הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁיִּהְיֶה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה.
and through this we rectify all eating throughout the entire year so that it be in holiness.
וְזֶה שֶׁאָמְרוּ
And this is what they said
(מְגִילָּה י"ג:)
(Megillah 13b)
בְּקִטְרוּג הָמָן שֶׁאָמַר:
regarding Haman's accusation, when he said:
וְאֶת דָּתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ אֵינָם עֹשִׂים — דְּמַפְּקִי לְכוּלָּא שַׁתָּא בְּ"שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם, פֶּסַח הַיּוֹם".
"'And the laws of the King they do not keep'—for they spend the whole year saying 'Today is Shabbos, today is Pesach.'"
וּבִשְׁלָמָא שַׁבָּת יִתָּכֵן שֶׁהוּא תָּדִיר בְּכָל שָׁבוּעַ,
Now, regarding Shabbos, that makes sense since it occurs frequently every week;
אַךְ פֶּסַח לָמָּה הִזְכִּיר שֶׁהוּא רַק פַּעַם אַחַת בַּשָּׁנָה?
but why did he mention Pesach, which occurs only once a year?
וְיוֹתֵר הֲוָה לֵיהּ לוֹמַר סוּכּוֹת שֶׁהוּא שְׁמוֹנָה יָמִים, וּפֶסַח רַק שִׁבְעָה יָמִים!
He should rather have mentioned Sukkos, which is eight days, whereas Pesach is only seven days!
אַךְ הַמְכוּוָן שֶׁלּוֹ הָיָה לְקַטְרֵג לְמַעְלָה
However, his intent was to prosecute on high
(כְּמוֹ שֶׁנִּתְבָּאֵר כַּמָּה פְּעָמִים),
(as explained many times),
וְהָיָה הַקִּטְרוּג דְּמַפְּקִי לְכוּלָּא שַׁתָּא בְּ"שַׁבָּת הַיּוֹם, פֶּסַח הַיּוֹם"
and his accusation was that Israel excuse the entire year by saying "Today is Shabbos, today is Pesach"
שֶׁאוֹמְרִים שֶׁעַל יְדֵי אֲכִילַת שַׁבָּת וּפֶסַח מְבָרְרִין לְכָל הַשָּׁנָה שֶׁאֲכִילָתָן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
claiming that through their eating on Shabbos and Pesach they refine and elevate their eating for the entire year into holiness,
וּבֶאֱמֶת אֵינוֹ כֵּן: וְאֶת דָּתֵי הַמֶּלֶךְ אֵינָם עֹשִׂים!
whereas in truth it is not so—"and the laws of the King they do not keep"!
וְאִיתָא בְּמִדְרָשׁ רַבָּה
And it is stated in Midrash Rabbah
(אֶסְתֵּר רַבָּה ז', י"ב):
(Esther Rabbah 7:12):
יֶשְׁנוֹ עַם אֶחָד — שִׁנֵּיהוֹן רַבְרְבִין, שֶׁאוֹכְלִין וְשׁוֹתִין וְאוֹמְרִים עֹנֶג שַׁבָּת וְכוּלֵּי;
"'There is one people'—their teeth are huge, for they eat and drink and call it 'delight of Shabbos,' etc.;
אָמַר לוֹ הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא: רָשָׁע, אַתָּה מַפִּיל עַיִן רָעָה בַּמּוֹעֲדִים שֶׁלָּהֶם?
the Holy One, blessed is He, said to him: 'Wicked one, do you cast an evil eye upon their festivals?
הֲרֵי אֲנִי מַפִּילְךָ לִפְנֵיהֶם וּמוֹסִיפִים לָהֶם מוֹעֵד אֶחָד עַל מַפַּלְתְּךָ וְכוּלֵּי.
Behold, I will cast you down before them, and they will add another festival celebrating your downfall, etc.'"
וְלֹא הוֹעִיל כְּלוּם בְּקִטְרוּגוֹ, וְאָמַר
And his prosecution availed nothing, and he exclaimed
(מְגִילָּה ט"ז.):
(Megillah 16a):
אָתֵי מְלֵי קוּמְצָא קִמְחָא דִּידְכוּ וְדָחֵי עַשְׂרַת אַלְפֵי כִּכְּרָא דְּכַסְפָּא דִּידִי וְכוּלֵּי
"Your handful of barley flour [the Omer] has come and pushed aside my ten thousand talents of silver, etc."
וְהַיְינוּ שֶׁבְּעוֹמֶר נִתְבָּרֵר שֶׁאֲפִילּוּ הַדּוֹמִין לִבְהֵמָה גַּם כֵּן יֵשׁ בָּהֶם קְדוּשָּׁה,
meaning that through the Omer it was clarified that even those resembling beasts also possess holiness,
וְאָז בָּא הַתִּיקּוּן לְשׁוֹרֶשׁ הַפְּגַם בְּלֵיל פֶּסַח שֶׁהָיָה אֲכִילָה בִּקְדוּשָּׁה;
and then came the rectification for the root of the blemish on Pesach night, which was eating in holiness;
וְלָכֵן בְּפוּרִים גַּם כֵּן מִתְבָּרְרִין יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁאֲכִילָתָן בִּקְדוּשָּׁה,
and therefore on Purim as well Israel are clarified as eating in holiness,
וְלָכֵן בָּא הַמִּצְוָה בְּפוּרִים לִבְסוּמֵי בְּפוּרַיָּא, שֶׁבִּשְׁלֹשָׁה דְּבָרִים אָדָם נִיכָּר: בְּכוֹסוֹ וְכוּלֵּי, וּכְמוֹ שֶׁאָמַרְנוּ.
and thus came the mitzvah on Purim to become mellow with wine, since a person is revealed in three things—his cup, etc.—as we have explained.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Pri Tzaddik, Shushan Purim 2 — “Haman’s accusation was that they make all their days like festivals and say it is a meal of mitzvah, and he said that in truth their intent is for bodily pleasure. In the Gemara the wording is that they spend the whole year with ‘Today is Shabbos, today is Pesach.’ It seems the intent is to the meals; therefore he mentioned only Shabbos and Pesach and not Sukkos, which is eight days, because in both of them eating is written explicitly: on Shabbos ‘Eat it today,’ from which we learn the Shabbos meals, and on Pesach ‘Seven days you shall eat matzos’… so these two, on which they hang the whole year’s meals of mitzvah.” Connection: The same question why Haman named Pesach rather than Sukkos, answered here from the explicit command to eat, with Haman’s charge traced to the serpent’s first enticement through eating.

paragraphs.text: Megillah 16a — Haman to Mordechai's students: "What are you studying?" They said: "When the Temple stood, one who pledged a meal-offering brought a handful of fine flour and was atoned." He said: "Your handful of flour has come and pushed aside my ten thousand talents of silver." Rashi has no comment on these words.

paragraphs.text: Parallel: Tiferes Yosef, Pesach — “The Omer was of barley, animal food, which shows that it is not yet within human grasp… The mitzvah of the Omer shows that a person nullifies all his own grasp and understanding before Hashem, and this is a great refinement against the prosecutors, for prosecution can rest on a person only where human grasp rules, as the Zohar says, blessing does not rest on a thing that is counted… But the Omer, which shows that a person nullifies all his grasp, can win against all the prosecutors. So we find in Megillah 16a that Haman said, ‘Your handful of flour has come and pushed aside my ten thousand talents of silver.’” Connection: The same reading of the barley Omer and Haman’s lament, with a different reason: the Omer stands for setting aside one’s own grasp, the one place no accusation can reach.
